4c7b2e34f369929f.text: Within 24 hours after the blast, the permit's terms require the Army to start testing soil and wiping surfaces for lead at parks, public places and private properties whose owners agreed, but only inside the heavier of the final dust map's two levels.

findings.problem: The block says "the permit's terms require" the sampling and names the "final dust map", but the claim only says the Army must sample, so a reader would believe these details came from the permit when the claim doesn't say so.

592a8ab25a0d4460.text: The Army says the blast will send up a plume carrying lead that spreads through the air and settles on the ground. It tells people in the plume's path to stay inside. For Friday it had asked residents near two parks in Middletown to leave from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m., because the blast could break windows. Linn County's emergency office says the maps the Army drew for Friday's weather should not be used to judge the rescheduled blast.

findings.problem: The block adds that the plume 'spreads through the air', which the claim states only as 'disperses', and presents the Army's predicted effect as the block's own wording without attribution beyond 'The Army says' — but more importantly nothing in the claims says the Army 'tells people in the plume's path to stay inside'; the advisory claim covers the affected area, not specifically the plume's path.

The claim says the advisory tells people in the 'affected area' to stay indoors; the block narrows/changes this to 'people in the plume's path', which a reader would take as a different (path-specific) instruction.
